newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine business urges support for small firms.
newsitem.headline: Philippine business urges support for small firms.

text.p: The Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry, the country's biggest business group, urged the government on Saturday to support small and medium enterprises (SME) in face of the growing globalisation of the economy.

The group passed a resolution on the last day of its annual conference asking President Fidel Ramos to initiate the networking of SME groups for them to exchange services and other information on human resources development, financing, market access and technology sharing.

The Philippines recently opened the APEC Centre for Technology Exchange and Training for SMEs to serve as a warehouse for all information regarding small businesses in the 18 member economies of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC).
The resolution also called for the immediate enactment of the bill which will make it mandatory for government agencies to source a portion of their supplies from SMEs.
The group further asked the finance department to come out with alternative financing programmes for SME.
At the same time, the businessmen called for the resolution of the increasing traffic problem in Manila as well as development of the local capital market.
Small and medium businesses from the Brunei-Indonesia-Malaysia-Philippines East Asean Growth Area (BIMP-EAGA) also attended the meeting in the southern city of Davao.
About 42 billion pesos worth of joint ventures have been signed during the three-day conference.
